statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the very price path this score measures. Stress eases to 50 in the elevated band: Saudi Arabia deferred retaliation for the East-West pipeline attack at Baghdad's request, Iraq dismissed its Maysan operations commander and closed the Shalamcheh crossing with Iran, and Iranian President Pezeshkian said the Strait of Hormuz would reopen if the United States ends its naval blockade, with an Iran-Oman route agreement due to be signed in Muscat on Monday. Confidence is 85 on a complete evidence set re-verified against primary sources this hour.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, and the advance was broad across megacaps and semiconductors. Second, CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC Sunday, roughly five hours after the final slot of this horizon closes, so no slot contains a tradeable session and no danger window is published. Third, the accountability response to Friday's pipeline attack ran toward de-escalation this hour rather than toward retaliation. Stress stays elevated at 50 because triple-digit crude, a shut 4-5 million barrel per day pipeline with no repair timeline, and a 16 September FOMC decision that markets were pricing at roughly an 87% chance of a 25 basis point increase all remain unresolved into next week. Stress alone does not change the mapped state.
headline: Twenty hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84 and WTI marked $100.05, and the response to Friday's drone attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline turned toward de-escalation: Riyadh deferred retaliation at Baghdad's request, Iraq dismissed its Maysan operations commander and shut the Shalamcheh border crossing, while the 4-5 million barrel per day pipeline stays closed with no published repair timeline.
body:
This hour re-verified the full evidence set against primary sources and found the price picture unchanged, as expected across a closed weekend. The Nasdaq-100 quote page still shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high. VIX remains 15.84, down 11.21%, having settled near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The latest H.15 observation, for 10 September, still shows the 2-year at 4.56% and the 10-year at 4.95%, and Friday's reporting had the 10-year finishing just below 5%. WTI is marked $100.05, down 2.37%, with Brent $104.61, down 2.81%.

The material development this hour is the accountability response to Friday's attack, and it points away from escalation. Saudi Arabia condemned the drone strike on the East-West pipeline in the strongest terms but agreed not to retaliate for now at Baghdad's request, while reserving the right to take all necessary measures. Iraq confirmed the drones were launched from Maysan province, dismissed the province's operations commander, ordered an investigation and closed the Shalamcheh border crossing with Iran as a precaution. In parallel, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said in a Saturday interview that the Strait of Hormuz would reopen if the United States ends its naval blockade, and that Iran and Oman will sign an agreement on a shared route in Muscat on Monday before Arab foreign ministers, to be notified to the International Maritime Organisation.

The offsetting exposures are unchanged and keep Stress in the elevated band. The 1,200km pipeline that carries 4-5 million barrels a day, roughly 4-5% of global supply, remains shut with no published repair timeline, and Hormuz has been closed to commercial traffic since March. US diesel prices are at record levels. Friday's August CPI ran 3.4% year over year with core at 0.3% month over month, above the 0.2% consensus, and the CME FedWatch tool moved to roughly an 87% chance of a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September FOMC, up from 72% the previous day and about 50% a week earlier. That combination is an energy-led inflation and policy problem rather than an observed no-retracement price path, so under the risk definitions it belongs in Stress and Confidence rather than in Tail.

Shared Finviz context collected at 16:33 UTC was structurally usable with a partial collection status, the calendar section unavailable, and is delayed latest-session evidence only. It corroborated Friday's completed session rather than any live path: index futures up 0.80% to 0.93%, VIX futures down 8.41%, crude futures down 2.37%, seven of eight megacaps higher, and five of seven tracked semiconductors higher with a 1.75% mean gain. Treasury futures were marginally lower across the curve, consistent with the firmer yields reported Friday. No part of that context was used as evidence of current NQ structure.

Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure, so conditional Tail rises only from 6 to a ceiling of 12 as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates, and no slot reaches the 25-point block threshold. The reopen gap and Monday's Muscat signing both lie beyond this horizon and are carried as checkpoints, not as scored paths. The next assessment that sees a live session will score the observed path: a wide reopen gap that holds near its extreme with shallow or failed retracements would be the evidence required to lift Tail, whereas orderly two-way price discovery would not.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 17:00 UTC on 11 September to 16:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens inside the U.S. afternoon that followed Friday's inflation print, with Tail between 13 and 17 in mixed mode and Stress in the high band near 79 decaying as the event passed and volatility fell. Tail dropped to 7 at the 21:00 UTC futures halt and has since settled into a 5 to 6 band in normal mode across the final nineteen slots, tracking the closure rather than any directional view. Stress fell monotonically from 79 to 51 across the twenty-four hours, and Confidence held inside the high band throughout, between 85 and 89. No slot in the window reached the 25-point Tail block threshold.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, roughly five hours after this horizon's final slot closes. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then steps through 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 to a ceiling of 12 as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of the reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout, and no danger window is published because no slot contains a tradeable session. Stress runs from 50 down to a floor of 46 through the overnight quiet, then edges back to 51 as the Monday Muscat signing and the reopen both approach with their outcomes unknown. Confidence decays from 85 to 80 purely as a function of distance from the last verified market observation. The conditions that would change this picture are observable only after the reopen: a wide gap that holds near its extreme, shallow or failed retracements, and repeated extension.
